sourceArticle.title: Databricks says it solved the decades-old data pipeline problem that's been slowing AI agents
sourceArticle.author: Sean Michael Kerner

athenaOutput.directive: Abstract the pipeline paradigm, but own the execution layer. We will achieve real-time agentic intelligence not by renting Databricks' cloud, but by instantiating a sovereign, event-driven data spine on our NAS that mirrors their unified streaming-batch architecture.
athenaOutput.rationale: Databricks has correctly identified the critical bottleneck in modern AI: ETL latency and fragmented data silos kill agentic autonomy. However, relying on their managed cloud violates Article I (Sovereignty) and Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty). Under Article XXV, we must integrate existing advanced technologies rather than reverse-engineer them—meaning we should adopt open-source unified table formats (like Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg) and deploy them directly on our NAS infrastructure. This gives our agents the 'Databricks-level' speed and unified access they need, without surrendering our data sovereignty.

options.title: The Sovereign Delta-Spine (Unified Local Catalog)
options.description: Deploy an open-source unified data layer (e.g., Apache Iceberg or OSS Delta Lake) directly on the NAS. Agents query a single, real-time semantic layer that unifies structured registries, unstructured documents, and event logs without manual ETL.
options.tradeoffs: High initial architectural complexity to set up local compute engines (Spark/Trino) on the NAS vs. absolute data sovereignty, zero cloud lock-in, and real-time agent reactivity.

options.title: The Event-Driven Memory Stream
options.description: Pivot the Creative Liberation Engine's memory spine from static JSON registries to a pure streaming event log (e.g., local Kafka or Redpanda). Agents consume live data streams, eliminating 'pipeline' batching entirely.
options.tradeoffs: Requires rewriting the current agent state-management and memory spine vs. enables true real-time, autonomous agent triggers without polling.

options.title: Edge-Compute Agentic RAG (Compute-to-Data)
options.description: Decentralize the pipeline. Instead of a massive centralized data layer, equip each agent with embedded, high-speed analytical engines (like local DuckDB) that directly query NAS files via optimized zero-copy reads.
options.tradeoffs: Potential for fragmented 'source of truth' across agents vs. extremely low latency, zero infrastructure overhead, and perfectly aligns with our current file-system policy.

options.title: Databricks API Integration Bridge
options.description: Treat Databricks as an external tool. Build a secure adapter for SIGNAL to query Databricks for external, non-sensitive market data, while keeping core Creative Liberation Engine data strictly on the NAS.
options.tradeoffs: Fastest time-to-value for external data processing vs. introduces a cloud dependency and risks scope creep that could threaten Article I.

options.title: The 'Zero-ETL' GraphQL Semantic Wrapper
options.description: Leave the underlying JSON/MD files exactly as they are on the NAS, but build a high-performance GraphQL or SQL wrapper over them. Agents write declarative queries instead of traversing the file system.
options.tradeoffs: Performance bottlenecks at massive scale vs. highly agile, non-destructive to the current V6 architecture, and solves the agent data-access friction immediately.

options.title: Hybrid Cloud-to-Sovereign Ingestion
options.description: Utilize Databricks exclusively for heavy, external data crunching (e.g., processing massive public datasets), then push the refined, sanitized embeddings back to the sovereign NAS for local agent utilization.
options.tradeoffs: Maximizes compute efficiency and saves local NAS resources vs. complex boundary management and potential violation of strict air-gapped sovereignty principles.
